display.title: Episode 378: The Whispering Droplets and the Silver Mirror (Lag BaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Lag BaOmer show with two stories: a generous man whose new wealth turns him into a miser until a Rebbe's mirror lesson, and how dripping water taught Rabbi Akiva it was not too late to learn Torah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Lag BaOmer 5749, the yahrzeit of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. Uncle Yossi wishes everyone a happy Lag BaOmer and recalls the Rashbi's teaching of Ahavas Yisroel and achdus, and two brothers lead the Shema. The first story tells of Reb Avraham, a kind man who gives tzedakah and welcomes guests. He asks a visiting Rebbe for a blessing of wealth, and the Rebbe warns him that riches can change a person. As his business grows, he stops davening in shul and turns away the poor. When the Rebbe returns, he shows Avraham the difference between a window and a mirror: once glass is coated with silver, you see only yourself. Avraham does teshuvah and becomes generous again. In honor of Lag BaOmer, the second story tells how Rachel urged her husband Akiva to learn Torah at forty, and how drops of water boring through a rock showed him that steady learning can soften even a hard heart. Uncle Yossi closes by urging good resolutions to learn more Torah and do more mitzvos in the merit of the Rashbi.
display.lesson: Wealth is a blessing only when it is shared; and it is never too late to learn Torah, because steady effort, like dripping water, wears through even stone.
